answer: Three defects in tools/goban-scaling-capture.sh FIXED.  Re-stamp of the 8 T924 rows APPLIED (peak_rss_mb retired to null; regime_claimed/observed/mismatch stamped on every row; the wall_s/nodes/exit/head/artifact_bytes fields were verified sound and remain).  Regression tools/regression-goban-scaling-capture.sh WIRED into zig build test.  The 8-row ledger is now self-describing: every row carries the truth of what happened, not a guess.

defects.name: peak_rss_mb under-reports
defects.symptom: 3x2 probe live at 1,440 MB recorded as 46 MB; 4x4 at 50x the same.  Same order of discrepancy across the 8 T924 rows.
defects.cause: The sampler read `ps -axo pid=,rss=` filtered to $CMDPID (the direct child), then took the max over 1-second polls.  A child that forks (a zig solve has a thread pool, a python solve may have a child, a build has at least 1 sub-process) under-reports by 1-2 orders of magnitude because the rest of the tree is invisible.
defects.fix: Mirror the runner's walker (tools/runner:1239 _descendant_pids_ps): one `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,rss=` per poll, build a ppid->[pid] map, BFS from $CMDPID, sum RSS over the descendant set.  Peak across the run is the metric.  Single awk pass per poll — no fork, no extra processes, no extra latency.
defects.regression_arm: B (peak_rss_mb >= 400 MB floor when the child forks a 300 MB grandchild)
defects.red_first: Pre-T926: peak=309 MB (parent alone is ~300 MB; pre-T926 read only the parent).  Post-T926: peak=612 MB (parent + grandchild).  Regression exits 1 on the pre-T926 shape, 0 on the post-T926 shape.

defects.name: killed run writes no row
defects.symptom: A wall-killed, RSS-capped, or signal-killed run produced nothing.  Reading 'not measured' when the work was measured-and-lost — the exact loss shape the tractability question exists to surface.
defects.cause: The wrapper appended the row AFTER `wait $CMDPID` returned.  Any kill that fired during the run (most wall kills, all RSS-cap kills, all signal kills from the lane orchestrator) means `wait` never returned cleanly, the script aborted under set -e, and the append never ran.
defects.fix: An EXIT trap appends the row with whatever was sampled up to the kill.  killed_by is stamped (none | signal | wall | rss | cap) and partial is true when the row was written without a clean wait.  A clean exit stamps killed_by=none, partial=false.  The trap is idempotent (APPENDED_ flag) so a signal-then-exit sequence cannot double-write.  set -e + the wait line is wrapped in `wait $CMDPID_ || RC_=$? || true` so a signal-kill's exit code survives into the trap.  A degraded-mode stderr message fires when the python heredoc itself fails (e.g. WEIZIGO_SCALING_LEDGER points at a directory), so the data is recoverable by hand even when the append is lost.
defects.regression_arm: C (child SIGKILLs itself -> row with rc=137, killed_by=signal, partial=true)
defects.red_first: Pre-T926: no row at all in the scratch ledger.  Post-T926: row with the kill fields populated.  Regression exits 1 on the pre-T926 shape (no row), 0 on the post-T926 shape.

defects.name: regime comes from the arg, not the run
defects.symptom: T924 invoked the wrapper with `writes-off` for BOTH arms of its 4x4 comparison, so the writes-on arm was recorded as writes-off.  Corrected by hand in 4a80255's successor (regime_corrected: 'T914: wrapper was invoked with writes-off for both arms; this node count is the writes-on arm').  The defect would re-fire the next time a comparison is run.
defects.cause: The wrapper trusted the positional regime argument.  Nothing read the command line to verify the regime matched the solver's actual mode.  A caller passing the wrong arg (intentionally or by copy-paste) silently corrupted the row.
defects.fix: Parse the command for RETRO_SOUND (drives memo_writes=false in src/retro.zig:3260) and RETRO_DEPS (memo_writes=deps).  Stamp regime_claimed (the arg), regime_observed (from the command), and regime_mismatch (true on disagreement).  A disagreement is reported on stderr in real time so the operator sees it during the run.  The row STILL LANDS on mismatch — losing it would be the worse failure.
defects.regression_arm: D (claim writes-off, command does NOT set RETRO_SOUND -> regime_mismatch=true + 'REGIME MISMATCH' on stderr)
defects.red_first: Pre-T926: the row had no regime_observed or regime_mismatch field at all (KeyError on read).  Post-T926: row carries observed=memo-reuse, mismatch=True, and a stderr warning.  Regression exits 1 on the pre-T926 shape, 0 on the post-T926 shape.

regression.wired_into: zig build test (added under the T926 label; siblings T927, T572, etc.)

arms.name: null (clean child, no forks, no kill)
arms.expected: row with rc=0, killed_by=none, partial=false, regime_mismatch=false, peak_rss_mb matches child's actual RSS

arms.name: seeded-defect: TREE RSS — child forks a 300 MB grandchild
arms.expected: peak_rss_mb >= 400 MB (parent ~300 + grandchild ~300); pre-T926 reads only the parent and records ~310 MB

arms.name: seeded-defect: KILLED RUN — child SIGKILLs itself mid-run
arms.expected: row with rc=137, killed_by=signal, partial=true; pre-T926 writes nothing

arms.name: seeded-defect: REGIME MISMATCH — claim writes-off, no RETRO_SOUND in command
arms.expected: regime_claimed=writes-off, regime_observed=memo-reuse, regime_mismatch=true, AND a 'REGIME MISMATCH' warning on stderr; pre-T926 has no fields at all

regression.isolation: Scratch git repo + per-arm scratch ledgers via WEIZIGO_SCALING_LEDGER.  Live docs/infra/host/goban-scaling.jsonl is NEVER touched by the regression.  The CAP env var overrides the capture script path so the regression can be re-run against any earlier shape (e.g. for the red-first confirmation).
regression.red_first_proof: The pre-T926 broken script (reconstructed by hand from the original task brief, stored at /tmp/weizigo/t926-confirm/capture-broken.sh during validation) was run with `CAP=/tmp/weizigo/t926-confirm/capture-broken.sh tools/regression-goban-scaling-capture.sh` and exited 1; all four arms failed with the exact defect symptoms.  The same command against the live capture script (post-T926) exits 0; all four arms pass.

changes: peak_rss_mb: numerical value -> null (retired; cannot re-measure historical runs)
peak_rss_mb_retired_value: original value preserved for archaeology
peak_rss_mb_retired_reason: explanation string ('Ruling: a suspect number in an authoritative ledger must end up corrected or gone, not annotated forever')
regime_claimed: stamped from the original regime field
regime_observed: derived from the command (memo-reuse for all 8 — none of the T924 invocations set RETRO_SOUND, so all 8 actually ran in memo-reuse mode regardless of the arg)

regime_mismatch: 7 of 8 are True (T924's 'writes-off' arg vs the actual 'memo-reuse' command); the 1 writes-on row carries the T914 hand-correction (regime_corrected) and is also regime_mismatch=True (its observed mode is memo-reuse, not writes-on — a truth the hand-correction papered over, since the solver was actually run in memo-reuse)
preserved_unchanged: nodes — sound (from command stdout, nodes=<n> parser)
regime — original value preserved (so any reader still finds it on the field name they expect)
regime_corrected on the 4x4 writes-on row — preserved (T914's hand-correction is the actual ground truth for that row's recorded regime)

what_still_stands: The 4x4 row's regime_corrected annotation (T914's hand-correction) is now in tension with the post-T926 regime_observed=memo-reuse: the wrapper's regime arg was writes-off (and hand-corrected to writes-on by T914), but the SOLVE actually ran in memo-reuse mode (no RETRO_SOUND).  Neither the wrapper's arg nor T914's hand-fix matches what happened.  A future task may want to re-measure that 4x4 node count to settle which is right.

The 8 retired peak_rss_mb values cannot be re-measured.  The wall_s and nodes columns are sound, so any tractability question that keys on those (e.g. the L2 (proven 4x4 values) landmark) is unaffected.  Any tractability question that KEYS on peak_rss_mb has no historical data and must wait for a fresh solve.

The 4x4 wall (1231s, 1971s) is still the only measured wall at 4x4.  T929's 4x4.D3 projection sits on it.  A fresh 4x4 measurement with the fixed wrapper would yield a real peak_rss_mb, but the wall column would be re-sampled too (deterministic given the same build, but worth re-running for the wrapper's own future ledger row).
